questions.text: The Credo principle 'Norm of Conduct' states architects shall uphold ideals and follow norms of 'a noble profession.' What distinguishes this aspirational language from the Code of Ethical Conduct's approach to professional standards?

options.text: The Credo appeals to character and identity; the Code prescribes specific prohibitions and enforceable duties
The Credo is mandatory while the Code is optional guidance, which is not typically enforced by professional bodies
The Credo establishes legal liability while the Code is purely moral persuasion, lacking any enforceable measures
The Credo applies only to licensed architects while the Code applies to all design professionals, including those in training

rationale.b: Inverts reality. Code is mandatory law; Credo is aspirational commitment.
rationale.c: Reverses liability. Code creates enforceable obligations (PRBoA discipline); Credo informs character assessment.
rationale.d: Both documents apply to registered and licensed architects in Philippines; scope is equivalent.
rationale.correct: The Credo's 'noble profession' language appeals to professional identity and character—architects internalize and commit to principles. The Code's specific sections (2-a, 5-i, etc.) prescribe concrete conduct standards subject to enforcement. Credo = character appeal; Code = conduct rules.
rationale.takeaway: The Credo appeals to professional identity and character through aspirational language; the Code prescribes specific enforceable conduct prohibitions and duties.

questions.text: Which Credo principle most directly addresses the contemporary professional concerns of environmental stewardship and architectural heritage preservation?

options.text: Accountability—service to country and future generations, ensuring sustainable practices
Professional Excellence—merit reputation through quality work, adhering to the highest standards
Legacy—protect environment and preserve architectural heritage for present and future generations
Ethical Relationship—uphold highest professionalism in relation to society, fostering trust and integrity

rationale.a: This option reflects a common misconception. Review the source provision.
rationale.b: Professional Excellence addresses work quality, not environmental or heritage concerns.
rationale.d: Ethical Relationship addresses stakeholder professionalism broadly, not environmental stewardship specifically.
rationale.correct: The Credo's seventh principle, Legacy, explicitly states: 'I shall endeavour to do my duty in the protection of our common environment and the preservation of architectural heritage for the sake of the present and future generations.' This principle directly embodies sustainability and heritage conservation—modern architectural priorities added to the 2018 Credo revision.
rationale.takeaway: The Credo's seventh principle, Legacy, commits architects to protect the environment and preserve architectural heritage for present and future generations.

questions.text: The Credo principle of 'Respect' commits architects to protect colleague rights and confine criticism to constructive intent. How does this principle align with the Code of Ethical Conduct's Profession obligation (Section 5-g)?

options.text: Both prohibit any criticism of colleagues regardless of intent
Both prohibit false or malicious statements and require constructive purpose for criticism
The Credo requires constructive intent; the Code permits malicious criticism if truthful
The Credo applies only to verbal criticism; the Code addresses written statements only

rationale.a: This option reflects a common misconception. Review the source provision.
rationale.c: The Code also requires avoidance of false statements (not just truthful malice), mirroring Credo constructive requirement.
rationale.d: Neither document restricts criticism type based on verbal vs. written medium; both apply to all forms of expression.
rationale.correct: Section 5-g (Profession obligation) states architect 'shall not knowingly injure falsely or maliciously, the professional reputation, prospects or practice of another Architect.' The Credo's Respect principle states architects 'shall respect the rights and works of my colleagues... and confine my comments to constructive intents.' Both require honest, constructive purpose—no false, malicious, or purely destructive criticism.
rationale.takeaway: Section 5-g and the Credo's Respect principle both prohibit false or malicious statements about colleagues and require criticism to serve constructive purpose.

questions.text: The Architect's Credo was officially adopted through PRBoA Resolution No. 05, Series of 2018. According to the resolution and associated materials, in what year was the original Architect's Code of Ethics formulated that forms the foundation for the 2018 Credo?

options.text: 2004 (same year as RA 9266)

rationale.b: RA 9266 (2004) is the legislative framework enabling SPP documents but not the original ethics code date.
rationale.c: 2006 is referenced in PRBoA resolutions but not as the original code formulation year.
rationale.d: 2009 is referenced in discussions of reverting to original code, but the original was 1979.
rationale.correct: The original Architect's Code of Ethics was formulated in 1979 by the United Architects of the Philippines. The 2018 Credo builds upon and modernizes this foundational 1979 document while maintaining core ethical principles.
rationale.takeaway: The original Architect's Code of Ethics was formulated in 1979 by UAP; the 2018 Credo modernizes this foundational 1979 document.

questions.text: The Architect's Credo opens with the principle of Accountability, stating the architect's duty extends to God, country, fellowmen, and self. Which Code of Ethical Conduct obligation most directly aligns with this accountability to nation and fellowmen?

options.text: Obligation to the Client regarding faithful representation and confidentiality
Obligation to the Public regarding health, safety, welfare, and reporting illegal practice
Obligation to Fellow Architects regarding fair dealing and commission courtesy
Obligation to the Profession regarding upholding dignity and competitive fairness

rationale.a: This option reflects a common misconception. Review the source provision.
rationale.c: Fellow Architects obligations concern professional colleague relationships, not public accountability.
rationale.d: Profession obligations concern competitive integrity and professional standing, not societal welfare accountability.
rationale.correct: The Public obligation (Section 1, Code of Ethical Conduct) covers architect accountability to nation (government compliance, law observance) and fellowmen (health, safety, welfare, illegal practice reporting). The Credo's Accountability principle directly maps to the Code's Public obligation tier.
rationale.takeaway: The Credo's Accountability principle (service to God, nation, fellowmen, self) aligns with the Code's Public obligation (Section 1)—health, safety, welfare, and reporting illegal practice.

questions.text: The Credo principle of 'Professional Excellence' commits architects to pursue integrity through industrious dedication and merit reputation for quality and fair dealing. Which Code of Ethical Conduct section most closely reinforces this Professional Excellence principle?

options.text: Section 1-a regarding public health and safety responsibilities
Section 2-f regarding commensurate professional fees based on experience and standing
Section 5-a and 5-b regarding refusal to provide uncompensated services or compete on fee basis alone
All of the above reinforce Professional Excellence through different obligation tiers

rationale.a: This option reflects a common misconception. Review the source provision.
rationale.b: Captures only Client obligation aspect of Professional Excellence.
rationale.c: Captures only Profession obligation aspect of Professional Excellence.
rationale.correct: Professional Excellence spans multiple Code obligations: (A) Section 1-a demands quality work protecting public welfare. (B) Section 2-f requires fair fee commensurate with standing and experience, not underbidding. (C) Sections 5-a and 5-b prohibit free services and fee-based competition, ensuring quality through adequate compensation. The principle manifests across Public, Client, and Profession obligation tiers.
rationale.takeaway: The Credo's Professional Excellence principle spans the Code's Public obligation (quality protecting welfare), Client obligation (fair fees), and Profession obligation (no free services or fee-based competition).

questions.text: The Credo principle of 'Ethical Relationship' pledges architects to highest professionalism in relation to clients, colleagues, industry partners, and society. When compared to the Code of Ethical Conduct's four obligation tiers (Public, Client, Profession, Fellow Architects), which stakeholder group does the Credo uniquely emphasize?

options.text: Industry partners (suppliers, contractors, manufacturers) as distinct stakeholder group
Society at large as broader stakeholder than the Code's Profession obligation tier
Clients as primary stakeholder (Credo lists first in its enumeration of relationships)
God and family as personal stakeholder relationships outside professional obligations

rationale.b: Society is addressed through Public obligation in the Code; not unique to Credo.
rationale.c: Clients appear in both documents equally; not unique distinction.
rationale.d: God/family relationships are personal domain, not professional stakeholder addressed in either document's obligation framework.
rationale.correct: The Code of Ethical Conduct structures obligations around Public, Client, Profession, and Fellow Architects. The Credo's Ethical Relationship principle adds 'industry partners' (contractors, suppliers, manufacturers) as an explicit stakeholder group not separately articulated in the Code. Sections 3-4 address contractor and supplier relationships within the Public/Client obligations framework, but the Credo elevates these to distinct stakeholder status.
rationale.takeaway: The Credo's Ethical Relationship principle uniquely emphasizes industry partners (contractors, suppliers, manufacturers) as a distinct stakeholder group beyond the Code's four obligation tiers.

questions.text: According to the Architect's Credo, the principle of 'Sharing' commits architects to generously share benefits with whom?

options.text: Only with fellow architects and professional colleagues, ensuring that the knowledge remains within the professional community
Only with clients through discounted fees or pro-bono work, focusing on client satisfaction and community service
With colleagues, friends, and strangers alike—universal knowledge and experience sharing
With the profession through published research and academic contributions, fostering a culture of continuous learning and development

rationale.a: This option reflects a common misconception. Review the source provision.
rationale.b: Narrowly interprets Sharing as fee-related. Credo emphasizes knowledge, experience, and intellectual benefit sharing.
rationale.d: Over-formalizes Sharing. While publication is one avenue, the Credo emphasizes direct sharing of 'experience and experiments,' not just academic research.
rationale.correct: The Credo states: 'I shall dedicate myself to the pursuit of creative endeavour towards the goal of enlightened Art and Science generously sharing [benefits of experience and experiments] with colleagues, friends and strangers alike.' The 'strangers' language explicitly expands obligation beyond professional in-group to universal knowledge generosity.
rationale.takeaway: The Credo's Sharing principle commits architects to generously share knowledge and experience with colleagues, friends, and strangers alike—universal intellectual benefit sharing.

questions.text: How does the Architect's Credo differ from the Code of Ethical Conduct in terms of enforceability?

options.text: The Credo is fully enforceable; the Code is merely advisory, lacking the necessary legal backing to impose penalties
The Credo expresses aspirational principles; the Code establishes enforceable obligations subject to PRBoA discipline
Both are equally enforceable through identical disciplinary mechanisms, which ensures uniformity in professional conduct
The Credo is enforced by UAP only; the Code is enforced by PRBoA, creating a dual system of accountability within the profession

rationale.a: This option reflects a common misconception. Review the source provision.
rationale.c: Different mechanisms. Credo operates through peer recognition and character evaluation; Code operates through PRBoA formal discipline.
rationale.d: Both are enforced by PRBoA. UAP may promote Credo recitation, but PRBoA holds regulatory authority over both Code and Credo-based character fitness.
rationale.correct: The Credo is a character and principle-based commitment recited at oaths; it operates as an aspirational standard reinforcing professional identity. The Code is law under RA 9266, enforced through PRBoA disciplinary action. Credo violations inform character assessment; Code violations trigger sanctions.
rationale.takeaway: The Credo is aspirational principle-based commitment recited at oaths; the Code is enforceable law under RA 9266 with PRBoA disciplinary sanctions.

questions.text: According to PRBoA Resolution No. 05, Series of 2018, architects are required to recite the Architect's Credo at which occasions?

options.text: Only at the initial professional licensure oath-taking ceremony, which marks the formal entry into the profession
At mass oath-takings, IAPOA affairs, and Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture events
At annual continuing professional development (CPD) seminars and refresher training, to reinforce professional values
At client meetings to establish professional credibility, although this is not a formal requirement

rationale.a: This option reflects a common misconception. Review the source provision.
rationale.c: CPD is not mentioned in the Resolution as required Credo recitation occasion.
rationale.d: Client meetings are not professional occasions where Credo recitation is mandated.
rationale.correct: PRBoA Resolution No. 05, Series of 2018, explicitly mandates Credo recitation with 'vigor, passion, and hope' at 'special or important occasions, such as mass oath-taking, IAPOA affairs and Board's events.' This ensures Credo is regularly reaffirmed throughout professional career at key collective moments.
rationale.takeaway: PRBoA Resolution No. 05, Series of 2018 mandates Credo recitation at mass oath-takings, IAPOA affairs, and Board events—not CPD seminars or client meetings.
